analysis: The only change in docs/operations/provider-release.md is a documentation addition at head lines 632-636. It says the release lane runs scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py on every built binary before the handoff, and refuses a binary that imports Foundation's back-deployed Date.>= or Date.<=. The change touches no code, workflow, key handling, attestation path, coordinator contract or cache logic, so it alters no trust boundary. The supplied units (base lines 905-1126 and head lines 1-454) are surrounding release-procedure prose that the patch does not modify. I found no regression against TB-011, T-054, A-011 or A-017 (release and build qualification) or against T-041 (cache). The new text describes an added build-time gate that refuses binaries which would fail on pre-release macOS 27.2, which is an availability and correctness control and not a weakening. Unverified: whether scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py and its workflow wiring exist in this PR. They are outside the supplied evidence, so the claim that the gate runs is unverified. If the workflow does not invoke the script, the doc would overstate a control, but that is not shown here. The rollout and catalog-capacity text (64-approval bound, release omission order) is unchanged context. It describes coordinator behavior owned by the platform, so I cannot verify it here and did not treat it as a finding. No new attack surface was identified.
